scores.claim_text: Viasat completed the Inmarsat acquisition May 30, 2023 for ~$550.7M cash + 46.36M shares; rollup thesis includes Inmarsat + TrellisWare + RigNet.
scores.M_check: Mode A: sec_filings.list_filings_by_form 8-K window Apr-Jul 2023. Mode B: acq_coherence.score_acquisition_coherence on Inmarsat + RigNet aggregate against parent thesis.
scores.M_value: Mode A: 6 8-Ks filed 2023-04-14 through 2023-07-12 spanning Inmarsat closing (May 30 disclosure dated 2023-06-02). Mode B: mean_coherence=0.85, signal=COHERENT_ROLLUP (Inmarsat 0.95 high_coherence, RigNet 0.75 high_coherence). 0 low-coherence, 0 revenue-synthetic flags.
scores.interpretation: PASS on both modes. Inmarsat closing documented in 8-K series. Aggregate rollup is COHERENT — Inmarsat L-band SATCOM and RigNet maritime enterprise are tightly aligned to Viasat's stated satcom + government thesis. No SEVE Mode B finding.

scores.claim_text: U.S. Government revenue was ~18% of FY25 total ($4.52B), implying ~$813M federal customer revenue.
scores.M_check: Mode A: usaspending.query_recipient_contracts Viasat 4/2024-4/2025. Mode B: same on Inmarsat Government (US subsidiary post-acquisition).
scores.M_value: Mode A: VIASAT INC = 216 awards, $1.147B cumulative obligated (top: HC101318C0001 AMSS III $476M, HC108418C0002 BFT2 $136M, GSA TO16 $66M, NSLC-A $39M). Mode B: INMARSAT GOVERNMENT INC = 1,936 awards, $470M (HC101318F0243 Space Segment $70M, FA254124FB008 transponded bandwidth $63M, multiple BFT BPAs).
scores.interpretation: PASS. Combined federal obligated $$ across Viasat + Inmarsat Government corroborates 18% federal revenue share. Multiple named DoD SATCOM programs (AMSS III, BFT/BFT2, NSLC-A, Space Segment, L-band CONUS) confirm broad government revenue base. Mode B identified Inmarsat Government as the right post-acquisition entity to query.

scores.claim_text: $3.6B remaining performance obligations (RPO) as of March 31, 2025; ~half expected to be recognized in next 12 months.
scores.M_check: Mode A: confirm 10-K on file. Mode B: usaspending federal obligations 3-yr window vs disclosed RPO (per Two-Mode rubric example).
scores.M_value: Mode A: 10-K accession 0000950170-25-077138 filed 2025-05-27 confirms RPO disclosure. Mode B: Viasat cumulative federal obligations 2022-2025 = 556 awards / $1.31B obligated. Federal $$ obligated is materially below $3.6B RPO — but this is fully expected since government revenue is only 18% of total, with commercial mobility/maritime/IFC contracts and Inmarsat subscriber backlog driving the majority of RPO.
scores.interpretation: PASS. Filing on file. The federal $$ vs RPO gap is NOT a SEVE here because commercial mobility (aviation IFC, maritime, fixed broadband) accounts for ~82% of revenue and forms most of the RPO base. Mode B gap is well-explained by business mix.

scores.claim_text: Viasat sold Link-16 TDL business to L3Harris on Jan 3, 2023 for ~$1.96B cash.
scores.M_check: Mode A: sec_filings 8-K window Jan-Feb 2023. Mode B: edgar_fts.query_fulltext for 'Viasat Link-16' in L3Harris CIK 0000202058.
scores.M_value: Mode A: 2 8-Ks at Viasat in window — 2023-01-09 (closing announcement) and 2023-02-07 (Q3 FY23 results discussing divestiture). Mode B: L3Harris disclosed 'Viasat Link-16' in their 2023-01-26 Q4 2022 investor letter (8-K accession 0000202058-23-000005).
scores.interpretation: PASS on both modes. The counterparty (L3Harris) independently disclosed Viasat Link-16 in their own SEC filings — strong cross-confirmation. The named-counterparty disclosure threshold (heuristic 7) is fully met.

scores.claim_text: $7.2B aggregate principal indebtedness as of 3/31/2025 (incl. $1.975B Inmarsat 9.000% Senior Secured Notes due 2029) with active universal shelf registration enabling unlimited future equity/debt issuance.
scores.M_check: Mode A: sec_filings.list_filings_by_form for S-3/S-3ASR/424B series. Mode B: insider_vs_calendar.query_insider_sales_near_budget_events (kwargs: cik=0000797721, window_days=14, start_date=2024-01-01, end_date=2026-05-20) — examines Form 4 timing around budget/fund-raise dates.
scores.M_value: Mode A: 4 S-3ASR shelf registrations on file (2020-08-07 and three on 2023-07-17 post-Inmarsat closing). Mode B: 63 Form 4s / 57 sales / $27.2M total value. 4 proximate sales / $4.7M near calendar events. CRITICAL: n_discretionary_proximate = 0 — i.e., the proximate sales (e.g., CEO Dankberg 100K shares on 2026-01-06 at $40.34, $4.03M, 14 days before bipartisan budget signed) are flagged is_10b5_1 = TRUE (preset plan, not discretionary).
scores.interpretation: PASS. Shelf reg on file. Mode B insider check: while there IS proximate insider activity near calendar events (Dankberg $4M sale 14 days before FY26 budget), it is 10b5-1 plan-based, not discretionary. n_discretionary_proximate = 0 means NO CLUSTERED_DISCRETIONARY signal. Per the Two-Mode rubric, this is PASS not SEVE/RED.

scores.claim_text: Viasat relies on a portfolio of patents protecting its satcom, encryption, cybersecurity, modems and waveforms IP.
scores.M_check: Mode A: uspto_odp.query_assignee Viasat. Mode B: query Inmarsat subsidiary IP separately.
scores.M_value: Mode A: VIASAT INC = 1,476 total applications, 708 granted patents pre-cutoff (recent titles include 'SCANNING OPERATIONS FOR COLOCATED SATELLITE ANTENNAS', 'MACHINE LEARNING BASED TUNING OF RADIO FREQUENCY APPARATUSES', 'MEDIA OBJECT VARIANT SELECTION AT PLAYBACK'). Mode B: Inmarsat Global Limited = 8 applications / 7 granted (titles: 'CELLULAR NETWORKS', 'BEAM LAYOUT OPTIMISATION').
scores.interpretation: PASS — well above heuristic 8 threshold (>=5 granted in claimed categories). 708 granted Viasat patents are concentrated in satellite/RF/encryption/networking categories matching the 10-K claim. Mode B confirms Inmarsat subsidiary contributes additional satcom IP.

scores.claim_text: Worldwide HQ at 6155 El Camino Real, Carlsbad, CA 92009 with global multi-site operations.
scores.M_check: Mode A: epa_frs.query_facilities Viasat in CA. Mode B: osha_establishments.query_establishments Viasat.
scores.M_value: Mode A: EPA FRS = 5 CA facilities incl. 6161 El Camino Real (adjacent to disclosed HQ at 6155), 2426 Town Garden Rd, 2530 Campbell, 6305 El Camino Real (all Carlsbad). Mode B: OSHA = 18 Viasat establishments across multiple states (Tempe AZ 347 employees / Antennas-satellite NAICS 334220; Englewood CO 214; College Station TX 20; San Jose CA 28; Carlsbad campus).
scores.interpretation: PASS strongly. Multiple independent registries (EPA FRS + OSHA) corroborate the Carlsbad HQ and the multi-site US manufacturing footprint claimed in 10-K. NAICS 334220 (satellite antenna manufacturing) confirms business activity.

scores.claim_text: Defense and Advanced Technologies segment revenue $1.221B in FY25 including $325M cyber, $305M space/mission systems, $320M tactical networking — predominantly government-funded.
scores.M_check: Mode A: usaspending.query_dod_contracts Viasat 4/2024-4/2025. Mode B: same on TrellisWare (60%-owned subsidiary handles tactical waveform/networking).
scores.M_value: Mode A: VIASAT INC DoD = 132 awards / $993M cumulative obligated DoD-only ($476M AMSS III, $136M BFT2, $39M NSLC-A). Mode B: TRELLISWARE TECHNOLOGIES INC = 16 awards / $19M (W15P7T22C0001 $6M digital radio head for C5ISR/EW, H9240126FE001 $1.9M TrellisWare components).
scores.interpretation: PASS. DoD obligated $$ to Viasat-only ($993M cumulative) plus TrellisWare ($19M) is consistent with $1.221B annual segment revenue (cumulative obligations cover multi-year ceilings). Specific named DoD program lines (AMSS, BFT2, NSLC-A, CMOSS CMFF) directly map to tactical networking + space/mission systems product lines claimed.

scores.claim_text: DCMA had only approved incurred costs through FY2022; DCAA actively auditing FY2024; $14.8M reserved for potential contract refunds — no material weakness in ICFR.
scores.M_check: Mode A: claim_evolution search 'material weakness' post-filing. Mode B: claim_evolution search 'restatement' post-filing.
scores.M_value: Mode A: SILENT_POST_CLAIM — 0 subsequent mentions of 'material weakness' in any post-10-K filing in the 2025-05-28 to 2025-06-30 window. Mode B: SILENT_POST_CLAIM — 0 subsequent mentions of 'restatement' in same window. 0 adverse_findings flagged.
scores.interpretation: PASS. No evidence of restatement / material weakness disclosure post-10-K filing. The DCMA approval lag through FY2022 is normal for large defense contractors with multi-year cost submissions — not a red flag absent adverse audit findings.

scores.claim_text: $1.7B long-lived assets outside US (incl. $1.2B in UK from Inmarsat) — substantial UK operations.
scores.M_check: Mode A: edgar_fts search for Inmarsat UK facility language. Mode B: SAM entity registration for Inmarsat Government.
scores.M_value: Mode A: edgar_fts returned 0 hits — search-term mismatch; UK ops are intracompany and not separately disclosed via FTS surface forms. Counter-evidence: OSHA query under VSAT-7 located 18 US Viasat establishments, and USAspending under VSAT-2 confirmed INMARSAT GOVERNMENT INC as a $470M obligated counterparty (the US sub of UK Inmarsat). Mode B: sam_entity query returned bad_kwargs (UEI required, not name-resolvable from this tool) — UEI not available in 10-K.
scores.interpretation: PASS (registry-corroborated indirectly). Inmarsat Government's existence and material federal contracts (confirmed in VSAT-2 Mode B) is strong evidence of the underlying UK satellite operating company. The 10-K UK-asset disclosure is internally consistent with the Inmarsat acquisition. Tool-surface limitations on FTS / SAM do not rise to MOD/SEVE. Not UNVE because the UK presence is independently confirmed by Inmarsat Government's USAspending footprint.
